label: Source-reported values from NASA's experimental tables, and averages derived from them. Not GFL measurements.
question: Does the spread rate of the 5 cm SIBAL strips of Saffire-II inform the 40.6 cm SIBAL sample of Saffire-I?

proxy_check.what: burn length divided by burn time, against the spread rate NASA reports, on the samples where the table gives both

deviations.detail: Saffire-I table: 0.37 under a header in cm; Saffire-II table: '037 mm' in mm for the same fabric; Saffire-III table: '.33 cm'. Not corrected; the numeric value is not used.

deviations.what: width and length of the large sample
deviations.detail: Saffire-I table lists width 94 and length 40.6 cm; the Saffire-III table and NASA's operations note give 40.6 cm wide by 94 cm long. Read here as 40.6 cm wide, 94.0 cm long.
Saffire-II table and readme: 29 cm; Saffire-I operations note: 25 cm. The table value is used for the burn length because the table reports the burn length itself (29 cm).
The Saffire-II column headed 'Spread Length' holds values in mm/s; read as the reported spread rate.
Sample 2-6 has no material in the table; read as the row above (SIBAL), as the readme describes two SIBAL samples. Stated, not silent.

reasons: each run is a named row of NASA's experimental table for its investigation
small samples: spread rate reported by NASA; large sample: average derived as length over burn time. On the small samples the derived average is within 5 % of the reported rate
same named fabric (SIBAL cotton-fiberglass); thickness unit differs between NASA's tables (SAF-D1)
oxygen 21.5 - 21.7 against ~ 22.1 % (largest difference 0.6 points); flow 20 and 20 cm/s, both concurrent; pressure not in the tables
GFL's regime module covers opposed flow over PMMA; it says nothing about concurrent spread over fabric
width 5 against 40.6 cm, length 29 against 94 cm: the scale differs by design, it is the variable Saffire tested
no rate was measured by GFL from the Saffire images; all values are source-reported or derived from the tables
NASA's tables give no uncertainty; two small samples, one large

source_reported_comparison.primary_reason: One or more required gates remain partial.

quantitative_transfer.primary_reason: Critical evidence or bridge status is missing or conflicting; no physical incompatibility is inferred.

comparison.reading: exploratory: one large sample, two small ones, no uncertainties; the large-sample value rests on the assumption that the whole length burned; an average over the whole burn hides growth and steady phases

assumptions: the Saffire-I table gives a burn time but no burn length: the whole sample length is taken as burned in that time
burn time is taken as the time the flame travelled, although it may include ignition and burn-out
not_done: a rate measured by GFL from the Saffire image sets, which are public
the opposed-flow samples (the table gives no burn length for them)
Saffire-III at 30 cm/s (its table gives no burn time)
